title: Existence of the normalized common-stage tensor braiding satisfying its prescribed finite-stage equations
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $W$ any scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field. Use the intrinsic rational coefficient stages and their normalized scalar stage system [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages], and its literal pair category $C_W$ [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Let $M=(E,A),N=(F,B)\in C_W$. Use the specified common-stage tensor and comparisons of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $S=\operatorname{commonStageTensorObject}(M,N)$ and $T=\operatorname{commonStageTensorObject}(N,M)$, whose stages are respectively $EF$ and $FE$. For every finite coefficient subfield $L\subset\Omega$ containing both stages, let $M_L,N_L,S_L,T_L$ denote their specified scalar transitions and let
$$c_{M,N,L}:S_L\xrightarrow{\sim}M_L\otimes_L^L N_L,\qquad c_{N,M,L}:T_L\xrightarrow{\sim}N_L\otimes_L^L M_L$$
be exactly the prescribed commonStageTensorComparison isomorphisms, including both input scalar associators and the operationStageTransitionIso identifications. Write $\sigma^L$ for the prescribed rational Koszul braiding [def-sf-rational-common-tensor-symmetries], the rational localization of the coherent-reduction-normalized integral Koszul braiding [def-pod-integral-tensor-constraints]. Then there exists an isomorphism $e:S\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ such that for every such $L$ and every pair of stage inclusion proofs,
$$e.\mathrm{hom}=\bigl[L,c_{N,M,L}^{-1}\circ\sigma^L_{M_L,N_L}\circ c_{M,N,L}\bigr]\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}_{C_W}(S,T).$$
Here $[L,u]$ is the literal pair-category class (the operation called ofHom in the Lean signature). Endpoint identifications turn this equality into the signature's heterogeneous equality. Existence alone is asserted; the parent theorem proves uniqueness.

proof.text: Use the rational braidings $\sigma^L$ of the scalar-compatibility lemma: these are natural isomorphisms for all rational arrows and satisfy $\lambda_{LL';V,U}F_{LL'}(\sigma^L_{U,V})=\sigma^{L'}_{FU,FV}\lambda_{LL';U,V}$. The lemma refers to the localized integral braiding, so it supplies the specified pullbackTensorRationalBraiding, rather than a freely chosen symmetry. All its hypotheses hold for the arbitrary scheme $W$ and every finite coefficient field in $\Omega$. To pass from the actual scalar functor to the recorded stage transition, conjugate this square by operationStageTransitionIso. Naturality of $\sigma$ moves its two input components through the swap, and the inverse component pairs cancel. The resulting $\lambda$ is exactly rationalTensorStageComparison, which is defined by that conjugation.

proof.text: Choose $J=S.\mathrm{stage}\,T.\mathrm{stage}$, the finite compositum. Define $b_L=c_{N,M,L}^{-1}\sigma^L_{M_L,N_L}c_{M,N,L}$ at every common upper field $L$, with $\sigma^L$ the prescribed rational braiding [def-sf-rational-common-tensor-symmetries]. It is an isomorphism $S_L\to T_L$; its inverse is $d_L=c_{M,N,L}^{-1}(\sigma^L_{M_L,N_L})^{-1}c_{N,M,L}$. Thus $[J,b_J]$ and $[J,d_J]$ are well-typed arrows $S\to T$ and $T\to S$. The source tensor stages $EF$ and $FE$ have the same underlying finite subfield, since each is the smallest subfield containing $E,F$; no definitional equality of their presentations is needed.

proof.text:
Check the actual transition formula. Write $a^A:T_{LL'}A_L\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{L'}$ for the stage associator at $A=M,N,S,T$, and write $F=T_{LL'}$. Expanding the prescribed $c$ (tensor scalar comparison followed by the tensor of the two input associators), FamilyTower for rationalTensorStageComparison and the stage-associator cocycle give
$$c_{M,N,L'}a^S=T_{L'}(a^M,a^N)\lambda_{LL';M_L,N_L}F(c_{M,N,L}),$$
and the same equation with $M,N,S$ replaced by $N,M,T$. This is precisely FamilyTower evaluated at $(M,N)$: its two input associators are $a^M,a^N$ and its output associator is $a^S$. Substitute these two equations in $a^T F(b_L)(a^S)^{-1}$. The adjacent $F(c)$ factors cancel. Move $\sigma$ through the two input associators by naturality and through $\lambda$ by the scalar square of step 1. The remaining expression is
$$a^T F(b_L)(a^S)^{-1}=c_{N,M,L'}^{-1}\sigma^{L'}_{M_{L'},N_{L'}}c_{M,N,L'}=b_{L'}.$$
Every associator here is the specified one, including repeated indices; no transition functor at a repeated index is replaced by a literal identity.

proof.text: For any prescribed $L$ choose a common upper field $H\supset J,L$. Step 3 transports $b_J$ and $b_L$ to the same $b_H$, so the quotient definition gives $[J,b_J]=[L,b_L]$. Composition of pair arrows is represented by composition over one common field. Consequently $[J,d_J][J,b_J]$ and $[J,b_J][J,d_J]$ are identity classes, since $d_Jb_J=1$ and $b_Jd_J=1$. This also works when the reflexive scalar transition is only canonically isomorphic to the identity: the identity at a pair is the class of the identity on its reflexive transition. Set $e=([J,b_J],[J,d_J])$. Its hom has every required representative, hence the recorded heterogeneous equation after the prescribed tensor-object equalities. Inclusion proofs lie in a preorder and do not affect any class.

It adds and drops no hypothesis. Steps: step 1 conjugates the new scalar square to rationalTensorStageComparison, which lem-weil-rational-tensor-stage-coherence defines as that conjugation. Step 2 is elementary inverse bookkeeping. Step 3: I redid the tower calculation. FamilyTower at EF≤L≤L' plus the associator cocycle gives c_{L'}a^S=(a^M⊗a^N)λF(c_L). Then the scalar square and naturality of σ^{L'} give a^T F(b_L)(a^S)^{-1}=b_{L'}, keeping the specified associators at repeated indices. Step 4 uses a common upper field and quotient equality; the transport of 1 is 1, so the inverse classes are the identity classes. New node lem-pur-rational-braiding-scalar-compatibility (naturality plus λ_{B,A}F(σ_{A,B})=σ_{FA,FB}λ_{A,B}) is true. It is statement-only and strictly below the item, and it does not restate the parent.
